target.title: fix(openrouter): preserve completed music when stream cleanup fails
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for this PR.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenRouter music generation could return a failure after a complete audio stream and [DONE] marker had already been received, when best-effort stream cancellation rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completed audio result now remains authoritative while reader cancellation is still attempted and awaited. Risk: cleanup must still run exactly once and release the reader lock; the regression and runtime proof cover both conditions.

## User Impact

Users keep successfully generated OpenRouter music instead of seeing a cleanup error after generation has completed.

## Evidence

Node v24.18.0 production-entry proof used buildOpenRouterMusicGenerationProvider(), a native Response/ReadableStream, and only replaced the network transport seam. The underlying cancel callback rejected after [DONE].

Before on ec998a0f3fc:

    {"outcome":"rejected","error":"cancel failed","cancelCalls":1}

After on current upstream main plus this commit:

    {"outcome":"resolved","audio":"live-audio","lyrics":["live lyrics"],"cancelCalls":1}

Focused regression:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.test.ts
    Test Files  1 passed (1)
    Tests  14 passed (14)

The same test failed before the production change with promise rejected Error: cancel failed. Targeted oxfmt, direct oxlint, and git diff --check passed. The changed-check wrapper was blocked before reaching these files by current checkout plugin-SDK boundary DTS errors in packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts; full build/check/test are left to fork CI.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review the change; the behavior proof was run manually.

target.title: fix(gateway): reject non-object MCP app tool arguments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with an MCP App widget could send non-object tool arguments through the Control UI bridge when a widget calls a tool. Arrays, `null`, strings, or numbers could be forwarded through `mcp.app.callTool` toward tool execution even though sibling MCP entry points already reject non-object `arguments`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI MCP App bridge now validates optional tool `arguments` at the server-method boundary before building the `tools/call` operation. Omitted arguments still normalize to `{}`, plain objects continue through unchanged, and arrays, `null`, strings, and numbers fail before `runtime.callTool()` is reached.

The change is intentionally limited to the Control UI `mcp.app.callTool` bridge. HTTP MCP, node-host invocation, standalone MCP App parsing, tool listing, message handling, and valid object-argument tool calls are unchanged.

## User Impact

MCP App widget tool calls now follow the same object-only argument contract as the other MCP tool-call entry points. Malformed widget-supplied arguments fail predictably before app tool execution, while valid widget calls continue to work as before.

## Evidence

AI-assisted: yes.

User-realistic call chain for the affected path:

```text
MCP App iframe/widget
  -> ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts:268-272 bridge.oncalltool forwards params.arguments
  -> src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts:106-115 handles mcp.app.callTool
  -> src/gateway/mcp-app-operations.ts:141-145 executes runtime.callTool(..., operation.params.arguments ?? {})
```

Before this fix, the Control UI handler cast `params.arguments ?? {}` to `Record<string, unknown>` without a runtime shape check. After this fix, the handler accepts omitted/plain-object arguments and rejects invalid values before constructing the tool-call operation.

Focused gateway-bridge proof added on the final head:

```text
src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts
  does not replace a completed bridge response with a cleanup error
    payload: arguments = { city: "Paris" }
    expected response: success, content text = "shared"
    execution proof: runtime.callTool("demo", "shared", { city: "Paris" })

  rejects non-object tool arguments before executing app tools
    invalid arguments covered: [], null, "city=Paris", 42
    expected result: "tool arguments must be an object"
    execution guard: runtime.callTool is not called
```

Local after-fix test output:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ✓ MCP App gateway bridge > does not replace a completed bridge response with a cleanup error
  ✓ MCP App gateway bridge > rejects non-object tool arguments before executing app tools
  Test Files 1 passed (1)
  Tests 11 passed (11)
```

Sibling surfaces checked:

```text
src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts:100-105 already rejects non-object tools/call arguments.
src/node-host/invoke.ts:853-854 already rejects non-object arguments.
The standalone MCP App path is already parsed through the MCP operation schema before execution.
```
